steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Mix brown sugar, oil, molasses, and egg together in a large bowl.
Combine flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, and salt together in another large bowl; stir into molasses mixture.
Roll dough into 1 1/4-inch balls. Roll each ball in white sugar; place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until center is firm, 10 to 12 minutes. Cool on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Ginger Snaps
raw_recipe.description: Mom's ginger snaps recipe makes a classic, favorite cookie with few ingredients and few steps. These spicy-sweet cookies are truly a snap to prepare.

review.reviewBody: I don't understand how some people can change a recipe drastically and then only give the recipe 2 stars. If you're substituting "healthier" ingredients or cutting back on ingredients the turn-out will be a whole different recipe. In essence, you are then giving a low rating your new, much worse recipe than the original recipe. I followed this recipe to a "T" and the cookies turned out excellent. I even had people who claimed to never before like ginger snaps rave over these. Well done! Thanks for the great recipe. I wouldn't change a thing!

((UPDATE: I continue to make these fabulous cookies. I've discovered that the fewer cookies on the cookie sheet the better, as they will spread out a little more and crackle even better! Also, I recommend dipping only the tops in sugar - this way, they don't stick to the cookie sheet.)) Absolutely the best cookies I have ever made! I was so excited to see that they had actually crackled and they looked so pretty and tasted amazing! The recipe has oil in it so the dough may look a little different than you're used to, but I think this is what makes these cookies so wonderful. I doubled the cinnamon and ginger, and *very* lightly greased my cookie sheets (or you can use parchment paper, because they will stick otherwise). I baked them for 7 minutes at 350 F., and they were perfect - soft, crackled, and totally yummy!

Great old fashioned ginger snap! 
Some hints:
* Pour the 3/4 cup of oil into a measuring cup, then add the molasses to the 1 cup line, That way, when you pour it out, none of the molasses will stick to the measuring cup.
* Sift the dry ingredients together to mix the spices in well.
* Only sugar the top half of the cookies so they don't stick on the pan. Yellow decorator sugar looks prettier than granular sugar.
* Don't over bake. My slightly smaller (3 1/2/ doz yield) cookies took 10 minutes.
* I didn't have cloves and substituted allspice. They were just as good.

so easy to make. and they come out perfectly crackled. (i do love the taste of ginger, so i use 2 tsp ground ginger and 3 tablespoons fresh grated. They taste exactly like my British grandmother made.) Those who say it is hard to work with or greasy, —>just forget your traditional cookie doughs! I put the dough in the fridge for 30 min before scooping and rolling. Then roll in white sugar that is in a small round bowl( like a cereal bowl) place balls on silicone mat( smooth side) or on metal tray lined with parchment paper. i have done it both ways with same result. in Fact i keep the dough in the fridge for up to a week, baking 6 at a time in my toaster oven so that we have fresh hot cookies when we want them.

I liked it very much. I followed the advice of a reviewer adding double the ginger, with a pinch of cayenne. Good idea! I would make the cookies balls more like 3/4" and probably with a little less bake time.

Love these cookies on cold weather days! I doubled all spices as others suggested, and added a dash of cayenne for some extra kick. I made my cookies into about 1" balls, rolled in cinnamon sugar and baked for about 10 min. Perfect!
Very easy to make! Doubled the spices as others suggested. I used a small cookie scoop and put sugar on top only. Delicious. Will definitely make again.

These were good but you definitely have to follow the tips below and 1.5 the spices. I also turned my oven down to 350 because the first batch just nuked. 375 is just too high for cookies in my opinion. I refrigerated my dough for a while so they didn’t spread out too far and cooked them for 8 minutes and they were perfect! I will probably use this recipe again

Perfect! I did doubled all of the spices, and added a fourth of a teaspoon of cayenne pepper as well as a half a teaspoon of black pepper. 8 1/2 minutes for mine and they came out crispy, very pleased.

My brown sugar was hard as a rock, so I used my food processor to crumble it. Wow. It was like flour. I thought I screwed the whole recipe up. I measured more than a cup, guessing what might have been packed. And more molasses because I wasn't measuring careful. I thought the recipe was doomed. Made three dozen crispy cookies with a delicious flavor. I'll make these again with regular packed brown sugar to see if they turn out the same. I call this recipe FAIL PROOF

I did take the previous recommendations to double the spices and chilled the dough perhaps 15 minutes prior to making the balls of dough. Very simple, straight-forward recipe that yielded a lovely, spiced cookie.
These are the best ginger snaps I have ever had. Chewy and full of flavor. I had many people tell me these were the best cookie at the cookie swap.

I have been making this with my daughter weekly, sending them off to older college kids. Everyone loves them! The only change we’ve made is to pull them out at 8 minutes, giving them a chewey middle. Perfect for an easy fall treat!
Four stars because like others, I too feel that it needs the amount of spices doubled. Otherwise, they taste great and was very easy to make.

My balls of dough must have been too large because I only got 24 cookies from the batch. They are delicious. I am inexperienced with a convection oven so I'm uncertain what made them flatter than most pictures. Either way, I'll make them again!

These cookies are great! As suggested by other reviewers. I doubled the spices and the cookies were perfect. To make the cookies crisp i just left them in the oven for two extra minutes. They were perfecr.
easy instruction come out great every time. Make multiple time a year one of everyone’s favorites .
Needed more flour! I just added enough until I got a firm dough. Also the commercial gingersnaps add pepper so I always had some white pepper. Great!

EASY, quick and SO very good! These have become a staple in our house... a little TOO addictive. ;) After baking these several times, and loving them - I tried making a half batch because I was low on molasses one afternoon. I don't recommend the half recipe... something was off, and while they were still crispy & delicious, the cookies didn't "crackle" on top the way they usually do. Lessons learned! Thank you for this wonderful recipe!
Love this recipe
